answer: Proof-of-Place Mechanism. Each identity needs sustained physical presence at a certified installation, verified by periodic random spot-checks relayed through a local vertex. An agent must hold a registered position at a jetty, orchard, or similar site whose occupancy sensors attest continuous tenure. Registering one identity costs an attacker weeks of on-site residence per site, since forged check-ins fail sensor cross-validation. Mass registration multiplies that residency burden linearly.
